angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 232,364 km at 134.02 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.4614 +/- 0.0275 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 134.02 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.334 +/- 0.039 solar radii from Mann et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-1650 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract): 232,364 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.326 +/- 0.047 solar masses from Mann et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-1650 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3410 +/- 56 K from Mann et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1650 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mann et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1650 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-1650.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.904, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
